title: NASA Shares Image of a Galactic Smiley Face - Nautilus
gist: NASA shared a 2015 Hubble image of galaxy cluster SDSS J1038+4849 that looks like a smiley face. The eyes are massive galaxies and the arc is gravitational lensing.

insights.claim: Hubble's 2015 image of galaxy cluster SDSS J1038+4849, 4.5 billion light-years away in the Big Dipper, resembles a smiley face and was recently posted by NASA.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie

insights.claim: The two yellow 'eyes' of the smiley are massive galaxies, while the face and smile arise from gravitational lensing predicted by Einstein's general theory of relativity.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Illustrates lensing as an observable consequence of general relativity.
